title: Cauvery water issue: DMK members walk out from both Houses in protest
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) MPs on Monday (August 3, 2026) staged a walk-out from both Houses of Parliament protesting against Tamil Nadu being denied its share of Cauvery water. They also held a protest outside the Parliament on the issue. 

Parliament Monsoon Session: Follow LIVE updates on August 3, 2026

The protest is centred on the alleged violation of the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s directives, which dictates that Tamil Nadu should receive 9.9 TMC of water in June and 32 TMC in July, bringing the total to 42 TMC. However, the State has “not received a single drop” thus far in 2026. The Tamil Nadu government has also approached the Supreme Court on the issue. 

“The original demand of 7,000 cusecs based on the already existing backlog has to be released to us. We wanted the House to debate and pass a resolution on this,” Rajya Sabha MP P. Wilson said.

DMK MPs carried placards in both Houses of Parliament. In the Rajya Sabha, Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan named Mr. Wilson, among others, for carrying the placard. When their plea for a debate was ignored, the DMK MPs staged a walk-out. 

Mr. Wilson also blamed the Congress for ignoring the issue that he said affected nearly everyone in Tamil Nadu. “The Congress is not bothered about the problems of the Tamil Nadu. They are only talking about other issues, so we have brought to the attention of the Parliament that this issue has to be, you know, sorted out by the Union government,” the DMK MP said.

title: Across the spectrum, Bankipur’s voters say they have chosen a better alternative in the JSP
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
Voters in central Patna’s Bankipur Assembly constituency, hitherto a stronghold of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), expressed happiness that the Jan Suraaj Party’s (JSP) Prashant Kishor had won the byelection, with people from across all sections and castes, including Muslims, members of the Yadav community, the upper castes, and the Scheduled Castes (SCs), opting to vote for Mr. Kishor.

The BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin won the seat in the 2025 Assembly election for the fifth consecutive term by defeating the RJD’s Rekha Kumari by over 51,000 votes. Earlier, Mr. Nabin’s father, Mr. Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha, had held the seat since 1995. In May 2026, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Mr. Nabin, dedicated the ₹115 crore Mandiri Nala project to the people of the area, with the road that came up over it named after Mr. Nabin’s father.

“Despite that, the people of this area rejected the BJP’s candidate, Neeraj Kumar Sinha,” Deepak Sharma, a member of the Bhumihar community and a resident of Bankipur’s Mandiri area, which has always voted for the BJP, said. “Prashant Kishor was a better candidate and a better alternative. He always raised public issues with clarity and boldness. Unlike other political leaders who make lofty promises, he raised the simple slogan — vote for the future of your children. This is something really different from others,” Mr. Sharma added.

Many upper caste voters felt the BJP had taken its voters for granted since it had been winning the Bankipur seat for nearly three decades. “The BJP thought that even if it fields an ordinary party worker, the voters will give them their vote. The people of Bankipur have rejected this mindset. No one can simply impose an ordinary candidate and expect voters to vote. In the entire campaign, the BJP candidate hardly spoke anything. If he cannot speak to the public, how will he speak about our cause in the Assembly?“ Akhilesh Mishra, a member of the Brahmin community and a resident of the Sri Krishna Puri area, said.

In areas like Peermuhani and Daldali Road, where SC voters are sizeable in number, residents said Mr. Kishor personally visited these areas, met people of the SC communities, hugged them, and made them promise they would vote for change. “What we like is that he (Mr. Kishor) categorically told us that if the BJP people are giving money, we must take it, but should vote for the JSP. Our community thought there was nothing wrong in accepting his proposal, and we did this,” Bittu Kumar, a voter from Daldali Road, said.

The Yaarpur and Jakkanpur areas, which have voters from Other Backward Classes (OBCs), mainly members of the Yadav community, also chose a new candidate in Mr. Kishor as the Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) remained largely indifferent throughout the campaign.

“When the campaign was at its peak, Tejashwi Yadav-ji was on a foreign trip and only joined during the last two days of the campaign. We did not find much enthusiasm and eagerness in the RJD. None of its MPs, like Sudhakar Singh, Misha Bharti, Sanjay Yadav, and Manoj Jha, were visible in Patna during the campaign, whereas 40 star campaigners [from the BJP] were attacking the lone man, Mr. Kishor. Seeing this, we decided to vote for the Jan Suraaj Party,” Mangesh Yadav, a voter from the Yaarpur area, said.

The Boring Canal Road area, which has a significant number of voters from the Kayasth community, rejected the BJP’s candidate, a member of their own caste, opting instead for Mr. Kishor.

A resident of the Boring Canal Road area and a member of the Kayasth community, who was part of the BJP’s election campaign and continuously organised small meetings in support of the party, also voted for Mr. Kishor. “When I came out after casting the vote for Prashant Kishor, pressing serial number 9, I told my wife also to not press serial number 2 on which the BJP candidate was there, and press the number 9 button,” a Kayasth voter said, requesting anonymity.

In Kayasth-dominated areas, including Kadamkuan, Exhibition Road, and Rajendra Nagar, voters chose the JSP. Many voters expressed anger over the violence against, and arrest of, their children by the police during the Bihar Bandh on July 25, 2026 against irregularities in the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test-Undergraduate (NEET-UG) exam.

Large numbers of Muslim voters in the Sabzibagh area also opted to vote for Mr. Kishor, who held three meetings in the area.

“As everyone knows, our community votes for candidates who can defeat BJP. We did not find that calibre in the RJD candidate, while Prashant Kishor was the one giving the BJP tough and sleepless nights. So we held a meeting in the nearby masjid [mosque] and called every person from our community with a message to vote for a strong candidate,” Mohhamad Rizwan, a resident of the Sabzibagh area, said.

“This time, the people of Bankipur have sent a clear message that democracy cannot be taken for granted. Historically, Bankipur has always voted independently. At different times, it has elected representatives from the Congress, the Communist Party of India (CPI), and the Left, right-wing parties, the Janata Party under Thakur Prasad, and even independent candidates on two occasions. This time, the electorate placed its trust in Prashant Kishor,” Patna-based political observer Sanjay Kumar said.

“In my view, the central reason behind this outcome is that the voters chose change over the BJP’s long-standing slogan of development and stability. That preference for change ultimately translated into Prashant Kishor’s victory in Bankipur,” Mr. Kumar said.

title: Lower House clears legislation to increase strength of judges in the top court from 34 to 38 amid disruptions by Opposition; Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, Indian Statistical Institute Bill introduced
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Lok Sabha on Monday (August 3, 2026) passed a Bill to increase the sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court without any discussion as persistent protests by Opposition members over the police action against protesting students at Jantar Mantar and the alleged chadhawa chori (theft of offerings) at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya continued to disrupt proceedings.

Two other legislations — the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, and the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 — were introduced amid sloganeering in the afternoon.

Parliament Monsoon Session Day 11 highlights

The House was adjourned repeatedly during the day as Opposition members trooped into the Well raising slogans and displaying placards, forcing Speaker Om Birla to suspend proceedings first till noon, then till 2 p.m., before adjourning the House for the day following the passage of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026.

At the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) meeting, sources told The Hindu that Congress deputy leader Gaurav Gogoi, Chief Whip Kodikunnil Suresh and Samajwadi Party MP Dharmendra Yadav demanded that Home Minister Amit Shah make a statement in the House on the police crackdown on protesters and that the government initiate a discussion on the alleged embezzlement of funds at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, during which Prime Minister Narendra Modi could intervene.

The BAC allotted three hours each for discussion on the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill and the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, and five hours for the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill. However, there was no discussion on taking up the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA).

The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill replaces an ordinance promulgated earlier this year to raise the sanctioned strength of the apex court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India. A statutory resolution moved by Opposition members seeking disapproval of the ordinance was rejected by voice vote.

Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal briefly introduced the Bill, but with protests continuing, it was passed by voice vote without debate. The government has argued that increasing the court’s strength is essential to address mounting pendency. As of January 1, the Supreme Court had 92,101 pending cases. The legislation says the additional judges would also enable the Chief Justice of India to constitute Constitution Benches more regularly. Five judges have already been appointed following the promulgation of the ordinance.

Amid the disruptions, the House also introduced the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, and the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026.

The Indian Statistical Institute Bill seeks to repeal the 1959 Act governing the institution and incorporate it as a statutory body corporate with the President as its Visitor and a Board of Governors as its principal executive body. It also provides for an Academic Council headed by the Director to strengthen governance, research and academic autonomy while expanding the institute’s role in statistics, data science and allied disciplines.

The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, introduced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, seeks to replace the colonial-era 1891 law by recognising electronic, digital, virtual and cloud-based banking records as admissible evidence in courts. It also provides for digital authentication of records and empowers the Centre to extend the law to other financial sector entities. Both Bills were introduced by voice vote after Opposition members who had submitted notices opposing their introduction did not press their objections.

title: Opposition MPs protest over Ram Temple donation theft
author: Sreeparna Chakrabarty
content_html:
Opposition parties on Monday (August 3, 2026) continued to protest in the Parliament House complex against the alleged donation theft at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and police crackdown on the anti-paper leak student demonstrations on July 20.

Like last week, the MPs kept donation boxes near the Parliament entrance, ‘Makar Dwar’, to symbolise the alleged theft of donations at the temple and lined up around them to raise slogans against the government. Some MPs put cash in the box enacting the donations made and the “theft” that took place later.

Members of the Samajwadi Party who were present said till now more than ₹47,000 has been collected and the money would be donated to the Ram Temple at Ayodhya and a receipt would be taken.

The MPs had staged a similar skit last week, which had led to objections from Hindu outfits and the BJP who alleged that it was an insult to ‘Sanatan Dharma’.

Parliament Monsoon Session: Follow LIVE updates on August 3, 2026

Shah’s absence

The Opposition MPs also protested against the “absence” of Union Home Minister Amit Shah from both the Houses of Parliament.

The protesting MPs lined up behind a big banner that read ‘Why Amit Shah is absent from Parliament?’.

Congress’ Priyanka Gandhi, SP’s Dimple Yadav and Dharmendra Yadav, Trinamool Congress’ Mahua Moitra, Jarkhand Mukti Morcha’s Mahua Maji, Revolutionary Socialist Party’s N.K. Premachandran, were among those who were seen at the protest.

They also raised slogans against Mr. Shah on the use of force against student protesters at the anti-paper leak agitation in the national capital last week.

“Modiji should apologise, for lathi-charging and firing pellet guns at the youth...but instead of coming to Parliament, he is intimidating and threatening the children. They do not come to the House, they do not answer questions, they do not speak on the theft of donations for Shri Ram Mandir, nor do they say anything on the suppression of students. Innocent children are not traitors, do not label them as such, the real traitors are the BJP people! who are crushing democracy,” Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said.

Questioning the absence of Mr. Shah from the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, Congress general secretary organisation K.C. Venugopal said: “Why is the Home Minister not coming to Parliament? In all previous sessions, he used to be very active. Then why is he not attending this session? The atrocities and attacks against students are still continuing. We, and the entire country, need an answer from the Home Minister.”

“Our protests outside Parliament, and on the floor of both Houses, will continue until the government is held accountable,” he added.

INDIA bloc MPs have stalled both Houses of Parliament over the twin issues with Bills being passed without a debate.

title: SC summons top Arunachal officials to explain ‘non-cooperation’ with CBI probe
author: Aaratrika Bhaumik
content_html:
The Supreme Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) summoned the Arunachal Pradesh Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary (Home) after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) alleged that the State government had failed to cooperate with its probe into allegations that Chief Minister Pema Khandu had favoured firms linked to his family members in the award of government contracts over the past decade.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta was examining a status report filed by the Central agency pursuant to the court’s earlier directions when it was informed that the Arunachal Pradesh Government had not cooperated in providing records sought by the CBI during its preliminary enquiry.

Taking note of the agency’s report, the Bench directed both senior officials to appear before it on August 24, 2026, and explain the State government’s alleged failure to comply with the court’s earlier directions.

“We deem it appropriate to issue notice to the Chief Secretary, State of Arunachal Pradesh, and the Principal Secretary (Home), Government of Arunachal Pradesh, making it returnable on August 24, 2026. Both the aforesaid officers shall remain present before this court along with their response to the aforementioned report of the CBI, and also explain as to why there is non-cooperation and non-compliance with the directions issued by this court,” the Bench said.

The order was passed in a public interest litigation filed by the Save Mon Region Federation and Voluntary Arunachal Sena, alleging that several high value contracts for development works in Tawang district were awarded to firms linked to the Chief Minister and his family members. The petitioners have alleged favouritism in the award of these contracts and sought an independent investigation into the matter.

Earlier, the top court had directed the State government to produce records relating to all contracts awarded across Arunachal Pradesh to the firms named in the petition.

On Monday (August 3), Justice Mehta questioned Additional Solicitor General K.M. Nataraj, appearing for the CBI, on the progress of the preliminary enquiry and asked whether the agency was giving a “long rope” to the Chief Minister despite having collected sufficient material.

Mr. Nataraj informed the Bench that the State government had not been cooperating with the inquiry and was yet to furnish all the documents sought by the agency. “The government is yet to furnish all the requisite documents... We will initiate steps in the proper manner. Let the State government cooperate,” he submitted.

Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the petitioners, urged the court to direct the CBI to register a First Information Report (FIR), contending that the agency’s preliminary enquiry had already revealed prima facie material indicating irregularities in the award of government contracts.

“Normally, a preliminary enquiry is only for the purpose of deciding whether an FIR should be registered or not... Coercive steps have to be taken,” Mr. Bhushan submitted.

Justice Mehta also referred to the discrepancies recorded in the CBI’s status report and questioned why an FIR had not yet been registered despite the material already gathered by the agency.

“In your report, it says all discrepancies. None of the procurement manuals has been followed... Oral work orders, no approval records, nothing. Why do you need anything more? You are just giving a long rope,” Justice Mehta remarked.

Mr. Nataraj clarified that the agency would take appropriate action once all the requisite records had been furnished by the State government. Taking note of the submission and the CBI’s allegation of non-cooperation, the Bench directed the top State officials to remain personally present before the court on the next date of hearing on August 24, 2026.

Earlier, the top court had directed the CBI to conduct a preliminary enquiry into the allegations concerning the award of public works in Arunachal Pradesh between January 1, 2015 and December 31, 2025. The agency was asked to examine why open tenders were allegedly not invited for certain works, whether the absence of competitive bidding affected transparency in the award of contracts, and the flow of funds and payments made under them.

The court had also permitted the agency to examine the beneficial ownership of firms allegedly linked to Mr. Khandu, and the movement of funds through such entities.

The petitioners had also relied on observations made by the Comptroller and Auditor General in earlier proceedings before the apex court, pointing to alleged departures from the General Financial Rules, 2017; the Manual for Procurement of Consultancy and Other Services; and the Manual for Procurement of Works in the award of contracts. The procurement framework, they pointed out, prescribes safeguards concerning the integrity of the bidding process, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, independence, and transparency at different stages of procurement.

The State government, however, has relied on a law enacted in 2015 that permits awarding contracts for work costing up to ₹50 lakh through a “work order” where no special technical know-how is required. It has maintained that the practice was followed with the objective of generating employment opportunities for local villagers and contractors.

“We deem it appropriate to issue notice to the Chief Secretary, State of Arunachal Pradesh, and the Principal Secretary (Home), Government of Arunachal Pradesh, making it returnable on August 24, 2026. title: IAF Chief begins three-day visit to Vietnam to boost defence cooperation
author: Saurabh Trivedi
content_html:
Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, Chief of the Air Staff, on Monday (August 3, 2026) began a three-day official visit to Vietnam aimed at further strengthening defence ties and expanding military cooperation between the two countries.

On his arrival in Hanoi, Air Chief Marshal Singh met India’s Ambassador to Vietnam, Tshering W. Sherpa, who briefed him on the evolving India-Vietnam bilateral relationship ahead of his official engagements.

The IAF chief was accorded a ceremonial welcome by the Air Defence–Air Force Service of the Vietnam People’s Army before holding bilateral talks with Lieutenant-General Vu Hong Son, Commander of the Air Defence–Air Force Service.

During the discussions, the two sides reviewed the progress of ongoing defence cooperation and explored new avenues to enhance collaboration, particularly in the air domain, as part of efforts to further strengthen the existing bilateral partnership.

‘Commitment to deepen partnership’

The visit underscores the shared commitment of India and Vietnam to deepen their enhanced comprehensive strategic partnership and reinforce defence cooperation amid growing strategic convergence in the Indo-Pacific region.

Recently, Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh stated that India has signed a BrahMos supersonic cruise missile deal with Vietnam.

title: Samyukt Kisan Morcha to meet all MPs, Ministers to campaign against trade pacts
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Senior leaders of the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) on Monday (August 3, 2026) said that they will meet all MPs and Ministers to campaign against the free trade agreements signed with United Kingdom and European Union and the one in discussion with the United States.

Maintaining that such treaties are not in the interest of agricultural producers and farm workers in the country, the SKM, the umbrella organisation of several farmers’ groups, urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to hold discussions with them before inking the deals.

“Moreover, such deals are not discussed in Parliament,” said SKM leader P Krishnaprasad at a press conference.

At a recent convention held here, the SKM had adopted a demand charter. The leaders said mass delegations of SKM will meet MPs and Ministers on August 17, 2026 to submit the charter of demands and to demand favourable action on seven principal demands.

The demands include repealing all free trade agreements, including the proposed Indo-U.S. deal and a law for legalised minimum support price as per MS Swaminathan Commission report and guaranteed procurement for all crops.

The other demands are: comprehensive loan waiver to end rural indebtedness and peasant and daily worker suicides; providing ₹25 lakh compensation to each peasant suicide victim families; scraping four Labour Codes and minimum wage of ₹ 31,000 payable to all workers; restoration of the MGNREGA, ensuring 200 days of work and ₹700 as wage; withdrawing the Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, the Seed Bill 2025, and the NFSA Amendment Bill.

It also is against forceful land acquisition and pro corporate land pooling and seeks protection of land rights based on LARR Act 2013, FRA 2006 of tribals and non-tribal forest dwellers and PESA 1996 on self-governance and tribal self-rule.

“The latest onslaught is the duopoly — of Adani and Leap India — in the FCI silos, where 77.5% of the grains will be controlled by them, along with the curtailment of free grains under the Food Security Act. Though not a single rupee of the farmers was waived, corporate dues worth ₹16 lakh crores have been written off,” the leaders alleged.

title: Baghel asks workers to beware of ‘traitors’ within Punjab Congress
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Amid its ongoing mass mobilisation programme at the booth level in the run-up to the 2027 Assembly poll, Congress’s general secretary in-charge for Punjab Bhupesh Baghel on Monday (August 3, 2026) cautioned party workers to stay alert against “traitors within the party who could cause serious damage”.

Addressing the gathering in Bathinda, he said the next elections will not be fought by the candidates alone, but by the entire party’s rank and file, underlining the need for strengthening the organisation at the grassroots level.

Warning against the “traitors within”, he quoted senior party leader Rahul Gandhi, who he said often “warned against the sleeper cells of other parties within the Congress”. The event was disrupted after a section of party workers boycotted it and raised slogans in support of Mr. Channi. Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, though, hailed the raising of slogans in favour of Mr. Channi, saying “he was one of the senior and most respected leaders of the party”.

‘Remove AAP government’

Mr. Baghel said it was important to defeat and get rid of the Aam Aadmi Party government, which had not only pushed the State into anarchy, but had looted and robbed the State as well. He added that nobody was feeling safe in Punjab as “gangsters were running the roost and people were getting killed in broad daylight”.

The conspicuous absence of Mr. Channi, who is believed to be upset with the party’s revamp, from the event along with leaders from his ‘camp’, has triggered questions over the party’s internal cohesion.
